title: A tea house on the hillside
summary: A cedar pavilion and jade roof, with four feet that follow a sloped stone island.
prompt: In Polynite, create an editable Japanese garden study: A cedar pavilion and jade roof, with four feet that follow a sloped stone island. Compose existing operators as data recipes; keep relationships, materials and exposed parameters editable. Use the linked scene as a reference, invent your own variation, and preserve the current scene.
try: Choose the tea-house or high-roof variant.
Adjust floor_clearance, rise, curl and overhang; Play shows the feet following the slope.
Save your version; Reset returns to the selected reference.
steps: Compose shared geometry and material operators from the recipe JSON.
Bind explicit supports or paths where needed, retaining stable IDs.
Expose parameters; verify changes, relationships and playback before saving.
settings: Open & test > Variant for presets; Adjust for recipe parameters. Scene settings > Living architecture exposes the same inputs. Support and path relationships are stored in the downloadable scene/recipe JSON.
limits: Stylised procedural study. Explicit analytic cube supports and flat named paths; no arbitrary terrain fitting or roof unions. Animation articulates cached petals; landscape changes occur at edit time.
